newsitem.title: USA: N. Carolina bank trustee charged with bond theft.
newsitem.headline: N. Carolina bank trustee charged with bond theft.

text.p: A former trust officer at First Union National Bank in Charlotte, N.C., faces charges of stealing more than $7.4 million of Arlington County, Virginia Public Improvement bearer bonds, federal prosecutors said Wednesday.
Kenneth Rocheck, 34, was indicted by a federal grand jury on charges of interstate transport of stolen financial instruments, bank fraud, embezzlement and money laundering.

The indictment alleged Rocheck used his position as senior trust officer to steal at least 42 of the Arlington County bonds with a face value of $5,000 each. The bank was the paying agent for the bonds.
The bearer bonds had previously been redeemed by other people and institutions and could be legitimately redeemed only once, U.S. Attorney Mark Calloway said.
The indictment said Rocheck created an account at another bank to deposit the redemption checks, using a false name and social security number.
Rocheck left First Union in June 1996 to take a similar job at an Ohio bank, illegally taking $7.4 million of Arlington County bonds and coupons with him, the indictment alleged.
If convicted, Rocheck could face up to 30 years in prison and a $1 million fine and could be ordered to pay restitution.
